archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (offense-led)
archetype.definition: A team that plays like one of the league's better sides on a per-play basis but sits at 3-4 because of close-game losses, giveaways and the worst special teams in football.

report.headline: A top-ten team in efficiency, dragged under .500 by giveaways and special teams
report.take:
The Rams are a 3-4 team that does not play like one. They rank 6th in net EPA, 9th on offense and 7th on defense, and lead the league in yards per game. Their point differential is positive and implies more wins than they have. A wins-over-expected mark of -1.59 sits 30th in the league. This is a McVay team with Matthew Stafford starting every week, coming off a 12-5 season in which it led the league in net EPA. The engine still runs; the record does not show it yet.

The offense is built on staying ahead of the chains. A 48.8% success rate ranks 4th. The line allows pressure at the 2nd-lowest rate and posts the league's best stuff rate. Kyren Williams and Blake Corum run behind it at 4.73 yards a carry. The passing game is only 16th in EPA, a long way from what it was a year ago. Stafford holds the ball 2.73 seconds, 25th, which suggests coverage is winning more often than the protection is losing. Puka Nacua has 62 targets in five games and Davante Adams is the clear second option, so the volume is concentrated where it should be.

The record is being shaped by three leaks that have little to do with down-to-down quality. The first is turnovers: 11 giveaways against 6 takeaways. The second is special teams, last in the league by a wide margin. The third is close games, where the Rams are .250. Losses by four to Denver, three to Buffalo and two to Arizona, the last as a 12.5-point favorite, are the record's real story. Special teams and close-game results tend to swing back toward the middle. Turnovers are partly a choice, given how often this offense throws relative to expectation (5th in pass rate over expected).

The real worry is on defense, and it is about bodies more than the numbers so far. The unit already generates little pressure (27th) and few sacks (27th). Now Kobie Turner and Poona Ford are on IR, Myles Garrett has played one game and is only nearing a practice window, Trent McDuffie missed the last game and linebacker Nate Landman is in concussion protocol. The coverage numbers have been excellent, including 2nd against deep passes. Whether that holds with a thinner front and a patched secondary decides whether this is a nine- or ten-win team or a frustrating wild-card chaser.

strengths.title: Offensive line runs the show
strengths.body: The line allows pressure at the 2nd-lowest rate and the Rams' runs get stuffed less than anyone's. That keeps the offense ahead of schedule and feeds a 4th-ranked success rate. This is structural, not opponent-driven: it held up against good defenses like Denver's and repeats the profile of last year's offense.

strengths.title: Coverage that erases big plays
strengths.body: Even without a pass rush, the defense ranks 2nd in EPA allowed on deep throws and 7th in explosive pass rate. It is also 5th on third down and 5th in red-zone touchdown rate. That is a disciplined, keep-it-in-front unit. The caveat is that McDuffie's absence tests it immediately.

strengths.title: Yardage machine with real volume
strengths.body: The Rams lead the league in yards per game and rank 8th in time of possession. They control games even when the scoreboard doesn't reflect it. That kind of efficiency usually converts to points over a full season once fewer drives die on turnovers and in the kicking game.

concerns.title: Giveaways outpacing takeaways
concerns.body: The offense has 11 turnovers and the defense only 6 takeaways. Turnover differential ranks 26th. Multiple giveaways showed up in most games, which points to an aggressive passing approach as much as bad bounces. Some of it will settle, but this offense leans pass-heavy, so it won't vanish.

concerns.title: Pass rush thin, then thinner
concerns.body: The defense ranks 27th in pressure rate and 30th in QB hit rate, and that was with Turner and Ford available. Both are now on IR, Ford for the season, and Garrett has played only one game. Elite coverage numbers built without a rush are fragile, and this is the concern most likely to get worse before it gets better.

concerns.title: Worst special teams in football
concerns.body: Special teams EPA per game ranks 32nd, and in a season with three losses by four points or fewer that alone can flip results. Special-teams play is volatile year to year and usually drifts back toward average. Until it does, it is a tax on every close game.

trend.note: Results have zigzagged: a blowout loss to San Francisco, then wins and close losses alternating, including the stunning home loss to Arizona. The Week 7 win in Las Vegas brought the best rushing day of the season.

nextGame.headline: A winless, broken offense visits a team that needs this one
nextGame.body:
The Chargers arrive 0-6 with the league's worst offense by EPA. They are last in passing EPA and near the bottom running the ball. Their line is 30th in pressure allowed and 31st in sack rate, the one matchup where even a depleted Rams front can win. Their defense is the real thing, though: 7th against the pass, 10th in pressure rate and 7th in takeaways. The Rams' ball security will be tested more than in most weeks. The Book has the Rams -6.5 with a 44.5 total, indoors.

Availability leans on the Rams' defense. McDuffie (groin) and Landman (concussion) both carry return estimates of game day, but neither is a sure thing. Turner, Ford and Garrett are out. For the Chargers, left tackle Joe Alt, safety Derwin James Jr. and receivers Ladd McConkey and Tre' Harris are all questionable. If Alt sits, an already leaky line protecting Justin Herbert gets worse.

waysToWin.title: Feed the run, avoid their strength
waysToWin.body: The Chargers defend the pass well but rank 27th in explosive runs allowed. The Rams' line wins at the point of attack, and Week 7's 199 rushing yards showed the formula. Leaning on Williams and Corum takes the ball away from a ball-hawking secondary and grinds a weak offense off the field.

waysToWin.title: Let their offense beat itself
waysToWin.body: Los Angeles ranks last in offensive EPA and 31st in sack rate allowed. Even a Rams rush without Turner and Garrett should get home sometimes against this line. Combined with a defense 5th on third down, short drives and field position should follow.

waysToWin.title: Take a shot over the top
waysToWin.body: The Chargers are stingy underneath but rank 24th in EPA allowed on deep passes. With the protection Stafford has, a couple of play-action shots to Nacua could break open a game this defense otherwise keeps tight.

waysToLose.title: Turnovers hand them short fields
waysToLose.body: The Chargers have 10 takeaways, 7th in the league, and the Rams give it away often. A winless offense can't sustain drives, but it can score off short fields. That is the most plausible way a 15-point-a-game team hangs around.

waysToLose.title: Another Arizona-style flat game
waysToLose.body: The Rams already lost at home as a 12.5-point favorite to a bad team. They managed 16 points while special teams and a stalled passing game let it stay close. If the kicking game keeps bleeding and the pass offense stalls against a top-ten pass defense, this becomes a one-score coin flip, where the Rams have been poor.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Rams stay patient on the ground against the Chargers' leaky run defense rather than forcing throws into a secondary that takes the ball away.

restOfSeason.body:
The efficiency is real and matches last season's profile, so expect the record to catch up with the play. The point differential already implies more wins than three, and special teams and one-score results are the stats most likely to drift back toward normal. The run game and protection should hold all year. The passing game has room to climb toward last season's level as long as the line keeps giving Stafford clean pockets.

Two things cap the optimism. The defense's pass rush has been gutted by IR moves, so its strong coverage numbers may slip, especially if Garrett's return slips too. The back half of the schedule is also hard: Kansas City, a road trip to San Francisco, Seattle twice against the league's 2nd-ranked defense, and Tampa Bay's 3rd-ranked defense. San Francisco's 6-1 start makes the division a long shot, so the realistic target is a wild card. The soft run of the Chargers, Washington and Arizona over the next three weeks is where that gets built.
swingFactors: Garrett's return and health of the defensive front
Special teams climbing off the bottom

confidence.note: Seven games, but the efficiency matches last year's profile; defensive injuries add uncertainty.
